findings.source_quote: For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the gospel: not with wisdom of words, lest the cross of Christ should be made of none effect. For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God. …it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe –1 Corinthians –1:17-21.

findings.location: Throughout source.html — all inline Scripture quotes (multiple … blocks)
findings.source_quote: Examples include: "…lest the cross of Christ should be made of none effect –1 Corinthians 1:17.", "For his letters, say they, are weighty and powerful; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible –2 Corinthians 10:10.", "Come unto me, …and I will give you rest –Matthew 11:28," "…If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink –John 7:37," "Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out… –Acts 3:19," "…we pray you in Christ›s stead, be ye reconciled to God –2 Corinthians 5:20.", "…to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ –Acts 20:21.", "…compel them to come in, that my house may be filled –Luke 14:23", "And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground... –Mark 4:16-17.", "For though ye have ten thousand instructors in Christ... –1 Corinthians 4:15-16.", "Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ –1 Corinthians 11:1.", "And we beseech you, brethren, to know them which labour among you... –1 Thessalonians 5:13.", "… have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul... –Hebrews 6:18-19.", "The wind bloweth where it listeth… John 3:8," "So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God –Romans 10:17."
findings.suggested_fix: All quoted Scripture passages must be translated into Urdu (Perso-Arabic script), preserving the exact verse references and their placement. Use conventional Urdu book names (e.g., متَّی for Matthew, متی/متیّ? — use the standard Urdu forms: متی (Matthew), یوحنا (John), اعمال (Acts), 1 کرنثیان, 2 کرنثیان, مرقس (Mark), لوقا (Luke), ابراہم/عبرانیوں? — use اعتدال: عبرانیوں for Hebrews, رومیوں for Romans, 1 تھسلنیکیوں for 1 Thessalonians). Do not leave English Scripture text or English book names. Example replacement for one: "…بَلاَ خُشْک دِلّی کے سبب جو لوگ سُن کر فوراً خوشی سے قبول کرتے ہیں اور اپنے اندر جڑ نہ رکھتے، وہ کچھ وقت کے لیے قائم رہتے ہیں: پھر جب کڑی پریشانی یا عتاب آتا ہے تو فوراً بے زار ہو جاتے ہیں — مرقس 4:16-17." Apply this consistently to every Scripture quotation, keeping the <em> tags and verse numbers unchanged.

findings.location: source.html — first body paragraph: parenthetical English terms and untranslated parentheses
findings.source_quote: "manger" and "swaddling clothes" in parentheses in English; also (Good Friday) appears in English within parentheses
findings.suggested_fix: Translate or provide accepted Urdu equivalents for parenthetical English words. Preserve parentheses and surrounding HTML. Suggested Urdu terms: "manger" → گھُنٹالہ/مَغزلہ (commonly 'مغزلہ' is rare; better: 'چرۂہ' or 'گھونٹالہ' but choose standard Urdu: 'گھانٹالہ' is nonstandard) — use 'خِستہ نَما چراغ' is bad. Simpler: translate 'manger' as 'چراغچہ/گودام' — better to use 'گھٹنالا (manger)' is inappropriate. To avoid inventing odd words, render both terms fully in Urdu without English parentheses: e.g., "کنواری ولادت، کھردرا گھوٹالہ (گودِ چوپائے) اور لپیٹنے کے کپڑے (swaddling clothes)" — but preferable: translate 'swaddling clothes' as 'لپیٹنے کے کپڑے'. For Good Friday, use established Urdu "جمعۂ عظیم" or "جمعۂ دکھ"; suggested: "جمعۂ عظیم (Good Friday)" if you must keep the English reference. Preserve tags.
findings.translation_quote: Original translation retained English words in parentheses: "(manger)", "(swaddling clothes)", "(Good Friday)"

For example, translate the Spurgeon quote into Urdu and then keep the English title/reference in parenthesis if desired. Ensure that any substantive quoted prose is fully translated into Urdu.
